group_assessment.weighting: A hepatology and pathology group studying tumour evolution by single-cell FISH; WWOX is one of eight probes and was added as a fragile-site marker. Not a WWOX group and not a neurological-disease group. Observation (counted signals per nucleus) is weighted above interpretation (WWOX loss as a novel NASH-HCC finding), which rests on four of eleven cases without a stated threshold.

entries.proposition: WWOX is reported as a copy-number loss in 4 of 11 NASH-HCC tumours; the readout is FISH signal number per nucleus with a BAC probe, not WWOX RNA, protein or any metabolic variable.
entries.snippet: We observed losses of WWOX, the fragile site marker, in 4 cases (36%).

entries.proposition: NO CLONAL COPY-NUMBER CHANGE, INCLUDING WWOX, IN ANY OF THE 11 NAFLD/NASH SPECIMENS: the steatosis and steatohepatitis tissue carries no WWOX loss on this panel. The WWOX signal is therefore a tumour (HCC) event here, not a steatosis event.
entries.snippet: NAFLD/NASH lesions did not show any clonal copy number changes for the miFISH probe panel applied.

entries.proposition: The most frequent aberrations are listed with MYC gain/WWOX loss in 4 of 11; no loss-calling threshold for a case is stated in the text.
entries.snippet: Observed aberrations were TP53 loss, TERT gain, MYC gain, MET gain, WWOX loss and HER2 loss/gain with TP53 loss (5/11; 45%) and MYC gain/WWOX loss (4/11; 36%) being the most frequent ones.

entries.proposition: Figure 3A (case 1, enlarged 2.5x): the WWOX row reads gains 1%, LOSSES 15% (highlighted red), average signal number 3.1, with the 16q row red across a large part of the tetraploid clones, and Figure 3B draws the terminal octoploid clone as WWOX-negative. Table 1 lists WWOX loss for cases 2, 3, 7 and 8 only and gives case 1 no WWOX loss, so the 4-of-11 count omits a case the paper's own figure marks (5 of 11 if counted), and no threshold is stated for what counts as a case.

entries.proposition: Figure 1: panel A shows three overlapping BAC clones (RP11-356N15, RP11-11M13, RP11-111D10) spanning about 78.94-79.39 Mb of 16q23.1 and a metaphase with signals; panel B gives the two probe panels with WWOX on the red channel in panel II. The probe is a custom 560 kb contig, so a 'loss' is loss of the signal from that region in a nucleus, not an exon-level deletion call.
